name: Deshi MCs

members.name: Mc Mugz (Syed Mohammad Sohel)
members.role: Rapper (joined after founding; later co-founded Jalali Set)

global_influences.evidence: Member SkibKhan is documented as hugely influenced by Tupac, Biggie, Eminem and Big L — a direct, explicit citation of core 1990s-2000s American hip-hop/gangsta rap figures shaping the group's foundational sound.
global_influences.source: The Daily Star — We invented Bangla Rap: Mc Mugz

local_adaptation_notes: Formed in mid-2005 initially as 'E.N.L.' (Enlightenment) before rebranding as Deshi MCs, the crew is widely considered the pioneer of the Bangla gangsta rap subgenre — MC Mugz has directly claimed 'We invented Bangla Rap' in press coverage — predating Stoic Bliss's more internationally-oriented diaspora hip-hop by roughly a year and representing a distinct, domestically-rooted origin point for Bangladeshi hip-hop alongside the Queens-diaspora lineage.
sound_evolution_summary: Founding period (2005): formed as E.N.L. by Mc Shaq, SkibKhan and Xplosive Flowrical, later joined by Mc Mugz and rebranded Deshi MCs. Breakthrough period (2006–2008): debut album Banned version 1 (2006) followed by the Jasper-produced collaborative album Kata Tarer Bera, whose single 'Ganjam' drove mass popularity; second album Banned version 2.0 (2008) extended the group's catalogue with tracks addressing hip-hop identity and social themes ('Banglai Hip hop,' 'Boma Hamla'). Later period (2017): returned with the single 'Bodybags' after an extended hiatus. Alumni note: Mc Mugz went on to co-found Jalali Set (2014) with Shafayat, directly linking Deshi MCs to the later, more folk-fusion-oriented generation of Bangladeshi hip-hop.
concert_culture_notes: Specific concert/festival data not yet documented in available sources — flagged for further research; the group's foundational role in Bangla gangsta rap likely shaped early underground hip-hop performance culture in Dhaka prior to the genre's later mainstream/streaming-driven visibility.
listener_community_notes: Considered the founding pioneers of the Bangla gangsta rap subgenre and a direct genealogical predecessor to Jalali Set via member Mc Mugz, making Deshi MCs a key origin node within the Hip-Hop genre's listener ecosystem alongside Stoic Bliss.
